headline: Kawhi Leonard (knee) will miss at least one more week.
body: Leonard is continuing the reconditioning process after receiving treatment to address swelling in his left knee, according to the Raptors. They’ll provide another update on Leonard a week from now. Ja’Kobe Walter will continue to start in his absence.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Kel’el Ware (ankle) is questionable for Tuesday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Ware popped up on the injury report Tuesday afternoon as questionable with a left ankle sprain. Potentially on the wrong side of questionable, some of Ware’s backup center minutes could go to Nate Ament if he’s ruled out.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Derik Queen notched 16 points (4-of-8 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), four rebounds and three blocks in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: Queen did most of his damage offensively in the second quarter, scoring eight of his 16 points. However, of greater importance to fantasy managers may be the three blocks, a new season-high and two shy of the second-year forward/center’s career high. However, his defense remains a work in progress, even with the blocks recorded on Monday. While Queen has been a consistently productive option for fantasy managers, the defensive issues are why he’s averaging 22 minutes per game and not more.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jeremiah Fears accounted for 11 points (4-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, eight assists, one block and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: Fears led the Pelicans with eight assists, but he also recorded six turnovers in Monday’s 138-87 defeat. This was one of his poorer performances of the season, and the Pelicans not having Trey Murphy or Zion Williamson didn’t help either. Fears will look to bounce back on Wednesday when the Pelicans host the Nets. That should be a better matchup for him than the red-hot Warriors were.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Dejounte Murray tallied 12 points (5-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: The Pelicans didn’t have Trey Murphy or Zion Williamson on Monday, and those absences were certainly felt. Murray shot a solid percentage from the field and led the Pelicans starters in scoring, but it wasn’t enough when the Warriors knocked down 21 three-pointers. Murray has been close to a top-50 player in nine-cat formats, but it’s fair to wonder if his presence in the lineup has limited Jeremiah Fears’ fantasy ceiling. That’s something to watch as the season progresses.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Anthony Melton amassed 16 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.
body: Melton was one of four Warriors to make at least four three-pointers in Monday’s blowout victory. With Brandon Williams suffering a hamstring injury in the first quarter, Melton is one Warrior whose minutes may increase if Williams misses time. Currently a player who should be rostered in deep leagues, some managers in 12-team leagues may be willing to roll the dice on Melton in the short term.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Yaxel Lendeborg produced 23 points (8-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.
body: Lendeborg continues to shine for the Warriors, making all four of his three-point attempts on Monday. The rookie forward has scored at least 20 points in six of 11 games and is considered by many to be one of the early favorites for Rookie of the Year. The Warriors play two more games this week, at Houston and San Antonio, so we’ll learn a bit more about Lendeborg in games of that magnitude.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brandin Podziemski amassed 25 points (10-of-19 FGs), two rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.
body: Podziemski shot 5-of-11 from beyond the arc on Monday, a season high for three-pointers in a game for the fourth-year guard. Even better for fantasy managers, Podz recorded a complete stat line, his third in as many games. Based on his ADP, Podziemski wasn’t expected to be a top-100 player this season. However, while it is early, he’s been a top-75 player in nine-cat formats.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Stephen Curry tallied 25 points (6-of-10 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, two assists and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.
body: Curry only played 21 minutes in Monday’s blowout victory, none in the fourth quarter. That’s all the time he needed to notch another career milestone, as the Warriors guard moved past DeMar DeRozan into 16th place on the NBA’s all-time scoring list. Thus far, Curry’s production has exceeded his preseason ADP by a safe distance, as he’s been a top-5 player in nine-cat formats. The Warriors end their week with games against the Rockets and Spurs, two teams that should offer up greater resistance than the Pelicans did.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Maxime Raynaud (knee) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Magic.
body: Working his way back from a right patellar subluxation suffered during the preseason, Raynaud was to be re-evaluated early this week. That did not happen on Monday, but the Kings are listing the second-year center out for Tuesday night. Precious Achiuwa and Dylan Cardwell have been providing depth at center when Domantas Sabonis is not on the floor.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Dillon Brooks finished Monday’s loss to the Spurs with seven points (3-of-14 FGs), four rebounds and one three-pointer.
body: While Devin Booker scored 32 points, no other Suns starter scored more than seven in Monday’s 122-96 defeat. Brooks had an especially rough night, as he shot 2-of-12 from inside the three-point line. While he managed a few rebounds, his poor shooting was compounded by a lack of assists and defensive stats. Brooks will look to bounce back on Tuesday against the Clippers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Luka Dončić accumulated 32 points (11-of-22 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, five steals and two blocks over 39 minutes to lead the Lakers to a 124-114 win over the Hawks on Monday.
body: Dončić fell short of the 40-point plateau in his return from a one-game absence due to a minor back issue, but showed no signs of rust, turning in another spectacular all-around performance that left him two rebounds shy of a triple-double. He scored 18 of his 32 points after halftime, helping Los Angeles withstand a late Atlanta rally before pulling away in the closing minutes. The Lakers were also without Austin Reaves (illness) in this one, making Dončić’s latest all-around performance even more impressive. The 27-year-old franchise cornerstone has been virtually unstoppable through the early stages of the season and has quickly established himself as the frontrunner in the MVP race.
author: George Bissell

headline: Onyeka Okongwu posted 16 points (6-of-11 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists and one steal over 30 minutes in Monday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: Okongwu was one of the bright spots for Atlanta in this one as he got off to an excellent start, knocking down a pair of three-pointers as part of a nine-point outburst in the opening stanza. He’s reached double-digit points in five consecutive games since the start of November and is averaging over 16 points and nine rebounds during that span. The Hawks will attempt to get back on track when the face the Bulls in a road matchup on Friday.
author: George Bissell

headline: Walker Kessler delivered 21 points (8-of-12 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block over 30 minutes in Monday’s win over the Hawks.
body: Kessler got off to an outstanding start with 15 first-half points and he managed to pull down just enough rebounds to notch a double-double for the seventh consecutive game since late October. The 25-year-old big man has fit seamlessly into Los Angeles’ nucleus after missing nearly all of last season following shoulder surgery.
author: George Bissell

headline: Nickeil Alexander-Walker tallied 20 points (6-of-19 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks over 34 minutes in Monday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: Alexander-Walker has been a consistent scoring threat for fantasy managers, scoring at least 20 points on eight occasions this season. He’s accomplished the feat in seven of his last eight games since October 28. He would’ve had an even bigger scoring performance had he not gone just 4-of-14 from three-point range in this one. The Hawks are back in action with a road matchup against the Bulls on Friday.
author: George Bissell

headline: Sandro Mamukelashvili chipped in 23 points (7-of-13 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and one block over 32 minutes off the bench in Monday’s win over the Hawks.
body: Mamukelashvili saw a massive uptick in minutes and offensive opportunities with Austin Reaves sitting out due to illness on the tail-end of a back-to-back for the Lakers. The 27-year-old drained 5-of-8 shots from three-point range and established season-high marks in both minutes and points. His fantasy appeal is strictly limited to situation-dependent matchups like this one where he receives extra chances.
author: George Bissell

headline: Jarrett Allen producted 12 points (5-of-5 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist, one block and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Hornets.
body: One of the few positives for the Cavaliers on Monday was that Allen hit his third three-pointer of the season. By comparison, he shot 3-for-41 from deep over his prior five seasons. Allen isn’t going to become a face-up center anytime soon, so there’s no need to entertain what that could do for his fantasy value. But he didn’t miss a shot from the field on Monday, which is a positive for fantasy managers rostering him.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Meleek Thomas finished Monday’s loss to the Hornets with 18 points (7-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, three assists, two steals, two blocks and four three-pointers.
body: With Cavaliers head coach Kenny Atkinson benching his starters for the entire fourth quarter, reserves like Thomas took on larger roles. The rookie wing scored 12 of his 18 points in the fourth, shooting 5-of-9 from the field. The 18 points were a season high for Thomas, who has scored in double figures in six of his eight appearances.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Donovan Mitchell recorded 11 points (4-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Hornets.
body: Like the other Cavaliers starters, Mitchell did not play at all in the fourth quarter. He and his backcourt partner, James Harden, had brutal first halves, scoring five points each while shooting a combined 2-of-13 from the field. They were more productive in the third quarter, but the damage was already done. The good news for fantasy managers is that Cleveland plays three more games this week.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Peyton Watson amassed 13 points (5-of-9 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Hornets.
body: Watson led the Cavaliers’ starters in scoring on Monday in arguably the team’s most disappointing performance of the season. Head coach Kenny Atkinson decided at the end of the third that he’d seen enough, so no starter played in the final quarter. Watson and the Cavaliers will look to bounce back on Wednesday against the Knicks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jeremiah Fears, Dejounte Murray, Herb Jones, Saddiq Bey and Karlo Matković will start Monday’s game against the Warriors.
body: The Pelicans are without Trey Murphy and Zion Williamson for Monday’s game, leaving two spots open in the starting lineup. Jones and Bey will fill the voids, with the latter being the better streamer for fantasy managers seeking offensive production.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Gary Payton II (knee) is out for Monday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Payton will miss Monday’s game due to left knee inflammation. His absence should free up additional minutes for De’Anthony Melton, who was already ahead of GPII in the rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Gui Santos (knee) is available for Monday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Santos is good to go after being listed as probable on the Warriors’ initial injury report. While he is likely to start, his reduced playing time makes Santos a player not worth the risk in most fantasy leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaylin Williams (back) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: Tuesday’s game will be the fourth JayWill has missed due to lower back spasms. Aday Mara has started two of Oklahoma City’s last three games, with Jared McCain receiving the nod in the other.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Robert Williams (rest) is not on the injury report for Tuesday’s game against the Thunder. W
body: Williams is back after missing Saturday’s loss to the Spurs. His return strengthens Portland’s center rotation and leaves fewer minutes for Yang Hansen.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jamal Murray, Christian Braun, Cameron Johnson, Aaron Gordon and Nikola Jokić will start Monday’s game against the Rockets.
body: All five Nuggets’ starters were upgraded from questionable to probable on Monday afternoon, and they’re now available. The Nuggets will roll out their usual starting five against the Rockets.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: DeMar DeRozan (back) is available for Monday’s game against the Rockets.
body: Upgraded from questionable to probable Monday afternoon, DeRozan is good to go. He’ll take on his usual reserve role, which has significantly lowered his fantasy ceiling.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Keegan Murray (wrist) is questionable for Tuesday’s game against the Magic.
body: Murray took a hard fall during the second quarter of Sunday’s loss to the Heat. That may be why his right wrist is sore. Murray came off the bench in his first game back from an ankle injury. If he can’t play Tuesday, Daeqwon Plowden or Jonathan Mogbo may get more minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, Julian Champagnie and Victor Wembanyama will start Monday’s game against the Suns.
body: The Spurs will be without Devin Vassell for Monday’s game, as he’s out with an adductor injury. Champagnie will fill the void in the starting lineup and is worth streaming, especially for fantasy managers needing three-pointers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Gary Payton II (knee) is questionable for Monday’s matchup with the Pelicans.
body: Payton II is averaging only 13.4 minutes per game this season, so his absence won’t significantly impact the world of fantasy hoops. De’Anthony Melton could see a few extra minutes in Payton II’s absence.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: DeMar DeRozan (back) and Cameron Johnson (lower body) have been upgraded to probable for Monday’s matchup with the Rockets.
body: DeRozan and Denver’s starting five have all been upgraded to probable, and the six are expected to take the court after returning home from Saturday’s win over the Pacers in Mexico City.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Nikola Jokić (elbow) and Aaron Gordon (lower body) are probable for Monday’s matchup with the Rockets.
body: Joker and the rest of the starting five were initially listed as questionable to face Houston, but the group plus DeMar DeRozan are all expected to take the court. Fantasy managers should keep an eye on the injury report ahead of tip-off for final availability confirmation.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Jamal Murray (shin) and Christian Braun (calf) have been upgraded to probable for Monday’s matchup with the Rockets.
body: Denver’s top six players were listed on Sunday’s injury report as questionable before getting this positive upgrade on Monday. The Nuggets’ starting five and Sixth Man DeMar DeRozan are all on track to take the court against Houston in a Western Conference powerhouse showdown.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Isaiah Joe (hip) is out for Monday’s matchup with the Wizards.
body: Izzy Joe will miss a seventh straight contest, and Kevin Huerter and Javonte Green should continue to see additional run in his absence.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Bilal Coulibaly (hand) is questionable for Monday’s matchup with the Pistons.
body: Coulibaly is dealing with left hand soreness, and he’s in danger of sitting out against Detroit. If Coulibaly is ultimately ruled out, Tre Johnson and Khris Middleton could handle expanded roles.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Devin Vassell (groin) is out for Monday’s matchup with the Suns.
body: Vassell will miss his first game of the season, which should free up more playing time for Julian Champagnie and Keldon Johnson. Both are work a look for fantasy managers in need of streaming assistance.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Morez Johnson Jr. (shin) is questionable for Monday’s matchup with the Pacers.
body: MJJ is a late addition to the injury report, and he’s in danger of missing the second leg of Dallas’ back-to-back set. The rookie has pulled down 26 total rebounds across his last two games, and if he’s ultimately ruled out, Naji Marshall and Santi Aldama could see additional minutes.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Collin Murray-Boyles (illness) is questionable for Monday’s matchup with the Grizzlies.
body: CMB is a late addition to the injury report, so his chances of suiting up against Memphis are in jeopardy. If Murray-Boyles is ultimately ruled out, Trayce Jackson-Davis and Kyle Anderson could see additional playing time.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Kyrie Irving (knee) is not on the injury report for Monday’s matchup with the Pacers.
body: Irving played in Sunday’s win over the Nets, and he’s on track to take the court for the second leg of the back-to-back set. On the season, he’s averaging 21.4 points, 3.6 rebounds and 4.4 assists across 29.5 minutes per game.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Quentin Grimes (finger) is out for Monday’s matchup with the Hawks.
body: Grimes sustained the injury in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s win over Detroit, and it will cost him at least one game. With Austin Reaves (illness) questionable, more minutes could be available for Collin Sexton and Jake LaRavia.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Austin Reaves (illness) is questionable for Monday’s matchup with the Hawks.
body: Reaves - who scored 43 in Sunday’s win over Detroit - is a late addition to the injury report, and he’s in danger of sitting out the second leg of LA’s back-to-back set. With Quentin Grimes (finger) ruled out, the Lakers will be thin on the wing, meaning Collin Sexton and Jake LaRavia could enjoy additional playing time if Reaves is ultimately ruled out.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Luka Dončić (back) is off the injury report for Monday’s matchup with the Hawks.
body: Luka sat out Monday with a back issue, although it may have just been precautionary since the Lakers play a Sunday-Monday back-to-back set. Austin Reaves scored a season-high 43 points in Sunday’s victory over the Pistons, but he’s now listed as questionable with an illness. Even if Reaves is available, he’s likely going to take a backseat to Dončić in the scoring department, as he’s done all season.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Moussa Diabaté (quad) has been downgraded to doubtful for Monday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Diabaté sat out Friday’s loss to Boston, and Ryan Kalkbrenner got the start. Kalkbrenner produced only four points and five rebounds across 21 minutes, while rookie Hannes Steinbach provided four points, 11 rebounds, an assist and three triples across 27 minutes off the bench. Steinbach is the preferred add, and he’s available in 98% of Yahoo! leagues.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Oscar Tshiebwe (illness) is out for Monday’s matchup with the Nuggets.
body: Even with Clint Capela (ankle) and Steven Adams (soleus) both out for the last three games, Tshiebwe has only seen 12 total minutes in that span. He can remain on the waiver wire in nearly all fantasy leagues.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Keegan Murray (ankle) accounted for 10 points (3-of-10 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), one rebound, two assists, two steals and one block in Sunday’s loss to the Heat.
body: Making his first appearance since October 23, Murray played a reserve role on Sunday. After playing stints of six, four and five minutes in the first three quarters, the Kings forward played the last 7:46 of the fourth quarter. Murray took a hard fall during the second quarter when he landed on his upper back after a Bobby Portis shot fake got him in the air, but he did not require any attention on the Kings’ bench. As Murray’s minutes increase, Precious Achiuwa (7/14/2/1 with one block) will likely see his minutes decrease after logging 36 minutes on Sunday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Zach LaVine recorded 15 points (6-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Heat.
body: LaVine shot the ball well on Sunday, but the playing time was an eye-opener. He played 25 minutes against the Heat and did not return after being subbed out with 4:03 remaining in the third quarter. The Kings made no injury announcement, and LaVine was called for one foul, so foul trouble couldn’t have been the reason. Kings head coach Doug Christie played Darius Acuff Jr. and Malik Monk (9/2/3/1) in the backcourt for the entire fourth quarter, which left no room for LaVine. That’s something for fantasy managers to watch moving forward.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darius Acuff Jr. tallied 32 points (11-of-21 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), five rebounds, 10 assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Heat.
body: Against one of the NBA’s better perimeter defenders, Miami’s Davion Mitchell, Acuff posted one of the best stat lines of his rookie season on Sunday. Shooting over 50 percent from the field, the Kings guard recorded his second 30-point double-double. While Acuff recorded five turnovers, he did a good job navigating the two-man game throughout Sunday’s defeat. The Kings play three games next week, starting with the Magic on Tuesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Davion Mitchell accounted for 17 points (6-of-11 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, 11 assists, one block and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
body: Playing against the franchise that selected him in the first round of the 2021 draft, Mitchell had one of his best games of the season on Sunday. In addition to recording his sixth double-double of the season, “Off Night” matched his season high with 11 assists. Rostered in 82 percent of Yahoo leagues, Mitchell’s fantasy value exceeds his ADP by a significant margin, and that may not change anytime soon.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Bam Adebayo produced 18 points (7-of-15 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, four assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
body: After a slow start to the season, Adebayo has scored at least 18 points in three straight and six of Miami’s last seven games. Against the Kings, he did most of his damage in the first half, recording a 16/5/2/2 line while shooting 6-of-9 from the field. In the second half, Adebayo took a back seat to Giannis Antetokounmpo and Klay Thompson, who combined to score 29 points. The Heat play three games next week, starting with the Jazz on Tuesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Klay Thompson amassed 23 points (8-of-15 FGs), two rebounds, four assists, two blocks and seven three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
body: Apparently, all Thompson needed to gain some semblance of consistency was to hit the road. He’s scored at least 19 points in three of the first four games of Miami’s five-game road trip, which concludes on Tuesday against the Jazz. On Sunday, Thompson shot 7-of-13 from beyond the arc, the third time this season he’s made at least that many triples in a game. Klay remains mainly a points and three-pointers option in fantasy leagues, but his assists and blocks were also solid against the Kings.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo finished Sunday’s win over the Kings with 29 points (14-of-23 FGs, 1-of-7 FTs), 14 rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks.
body: While Giannis had a brutal night at the foul line, fantasy managers rostering the Heat forward know they’ll likely have to punt on free-throw percentage. Against the Kings, he made up for the poor night at the foul line with excellent shooting from the field and big numbers in rebounds, steals and blocks. The Heat play three games in Week 4, starting with the Jazz on Tuesday in the final game of Miami’s road trip.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jeremiah Fears recorded 25 points (10-of-14 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Clippers.
body: Fears continues to spread his wings as the Pelicans’ point guard, scoring at least 19 points in three straight games and in five of his last six appearances. What’s especially encouraging for those rostering the second-year guard is that the return of Dejounte Murray (6/3/3 in 28 minutes) has not led to a decrease in production. Fears’ current fantasy value sits just outside the top-100, but that will change if he continues to play as he has over the last week.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Trey Murphy accounted for 26 points (9-of-17 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Clippers.
body: After shooting 12-of-28 from the field in his prior three appearances, Murphy made over 50 percent of his shots on Sunday. Add in the rebounds, assists and three-pointers, and this was a good finish to Week 3 for the Pelicans forward. The 26 points matched Murphy’s season high, and he’ll look to build on this effort when the Pelicans begin a four-game Week 4 on Monday against the Warriors.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Zion Williamson finished Sunday’s loss to the Clippers with 25 points (9-of-9 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), four rebounds and two assists.
body: Williamson produced excellent percentages in his final game of the week, much to the delight of those rostering him in category leagues. Unfortunately, the production outside of the points and percentages was pretty lean in the Pelicans’ 139-123 defeat. That said, over three weeks, Williamson’s production has exceeded his ADP (69) by a safe distance. The hope is that he can avoid the extended absence that has been a common occurrence throughout his NBA career.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Keyonte George (ankle) will not return to Sunday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: George sprained his right ankle early in the third quarter and has since returned to the locker room. With their starting point guard done for the night, the Jazz will rely more on Isaiah Collier and Darryn Peterson.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: X-rays on Quentin Grimes’ finger came back negative, Lakers head coach JJ Redick said after Sunday’s win over the Pistons.
body: Starting for Luka Dončić (back), Grimes left Sunday’s game during the fourth quarter after banging his finger. The good news is that X-rays came back negative. Fantasy managers should consider Grimes questionable for Monday’s game against the Hawks. If Dončić is available, Grimes will come off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Austin Reaves exploded for a season-high 43 points (14-of-27 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), five rebounds and four assists over 37 minutes to power the Lakers to a 121-116 win over the Pistons on Sunday.
body: No Luka Dončić, no problem. Reaves picked up the slack from a creation standpoint with the current MVP frontrunner sidelined by a back issue in this one. Dončić entered the contest averaging a league-best 40.1 points per game, leaving a significant void for the Lakers to fill. It wasn’t an issue for Reaves, who embraced the expanded offensive responsibilities, repeatedly getting to his spots and making Detroit pay in one-on-one situations from the mid-range. He poured in a team-high 19 first-half points to give Los Angeles a 13-point advantage at the break before tacking on 12 more in the third quarter alone. He drilled a crowd-silencing stepback three-pointer to give Los Angeles an eight-point lead in the final minute. It’s abundantly clear that his fantasy appeal rises exponentially whenever Dončić is out of the lineup. The Lakers continue their current road trip with a three-game week that includes showdowns against the Hawks, Bucks and Suns.
author: George Bissell

headline: Daniss Jenkins tallied a career-high 31 points (9-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, four assists and one steal over 32 minutes off the bench in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: Jenkins erupted for a game-high 22 first-half points, shooting 7-of-9 from the floor and 6-of-7 from three-point range in just 13 minutes off the bench. He capped the spectacular half by burying his sixth triple just over one second before the buzzer, sending the crowd into halftime with one final highlight. His sublime effort provided a much-needed lift for Detroit on an off-night for Cade Cunningham, who was held to just - points. The 25-year-old backup point guard knocked down 8-of-14 from three-point range, eclipsing the 20-point threshold for the first time this season. He doesn’t offer a ton of fantasy appeal in a bench role, but that could change if he continues to shoot over 40 percent from downtown. The Pistons have a three-game week on tap that features a pair of matchups against the lowly Wizards before a road tilt against the Heat.
author: George Bissell

headline: Walker Kessler recorded a double-double with 12 points (5-of-10 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), 16 rebounds, four assists, one steal and three blocks over 29 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Pistons.
body: The 16 boards were a season-high for Kessler as he recorded his fifth double-digit rebounding performance of his Lakers debut, taking advantage of the absence of Detroit’s powerful center Jalen Duren, who remains out with a hamstring injury. He’s notched all five of those efforts over his last six games since October 30. He came up with a key offensive rebound and converted a three-point play to give the Lakers a commanding eight-point advantage with just over two minutes left in regulation. The Lakers have a three-game week on tap that includes matchups against the Hawks, Bucks and Suns.
author: George Bissell

headline: Kevin Huerter went off for 24 points (9-of-14 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, two steals and five blocks over 35 minutes off the bench in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: Huerter provided a significant spark off Detroit’s bench, helping the Pistons claw back from a nearly 30-point deficit with 10 points in the third quarter. His most impressive moment of the period, however, came as a facilitator rather than a scorer, as he threaded a nifty no-look, over-the-shoulder pass to teammate Daniss Jenkins for a corner three. He also posted an unexpected five blocks as well. His sublime all-around effort helped make up for an off-night for franchise building block Cade Cunningham, who was held scoreless in the first half and finished with just 14 points. The Pistons have a three-game week on tap that features a pair of matchups against the lowly Wizards before a road tilt against the Heat.
author: George Bissell

headline: Cade Cunningham totaled 14 points (6-of-15 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists and two steals across 38 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: Cunningham was held without a basket in the first half as he cobbled together an uncharacteristically poor shooting performance, finishing just 1-of-6 from three-point range. He managed to somewhat salvage the effort from a fantasy perspective by still getting to double digits while also dishing out eight assists. He’ll attempt to get back on track when the Pistons kick off a three-game week with a pair of matchups against the lowly Wizards before facing the Heat in a road tilt.
author: George Bissell

headline: Domantas Sabonis (knee) ruled out vs. Heat.
body: Sabonis was a late addition to the King’s injury report, and will now not suit up vs. the Heat. Dylan Caldwell and Jonathan Mogbo, who is active for Sunday’s contest, will fill in for the big man.
author: Shawn Robinson

headline: Will Richard (thumb) is out for Monday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Richard has been diagnosed with a UCL tear in his left thumb and will, at a minimum, miss Monday’s game. Gary Payton II and De’Anthony Melton may absorb the minutes Richard would have gotten if he could play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Gui Santos (knee) is probable for Monday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Santos is on track to play Monday night. Although he started Saturday’s overtime win over the Magic, the Warriors forward played only 12 minutes. The Warriors will rely more on Georges Niang as long as Santos’ knee remains an issue.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Mike Conley, Derrick White, Paul George, Jayson Tatum and Neemias Queta will start Sunday’s game against the Bucks.
body: The Celtics have changed their starting lineup, with Conley replacing Jordan Walsh. Conley has appeared in three games this season, so his fantasy outlook isn’t the best, even with the spot start. The other four starters are unchanged.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jordan Goodwin (calf) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Spurs.
body: Goodwin has missed the Suns’ last three games with a right calf injury. If Goodwin can play on Monday, his return would likely result in fewer minutes for fellow reserve Ryan Dunn.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Devin Vassell (groin) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Suns.
body: Vassell is dealing with left adductor tightness, casting some doubt on his availability for Monday. Julian Champagnie could be the replacement in the starting lineup if Vassell can’t play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Mitchell Robinson (illness) is available for Sunday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Added to the injury report Sunday afternoon, Robinson is set to play. He’ll likely continue to come off the bench, with Neemias Queta starting at center.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Jackson (groin) will travel with the Clippers for Tuesday’s game against the Suns.
body: Jackson is missing Sunday’s game against the Pelicans with a sore groin. However, his injury is not expected to cause an extended absence, so Jackson will travel with the team for Tuesday’s game against the Suns. If he doesn’t play in that contest, his next opportunity to play would be Friday against the Thunder.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brandon Ingram (Achilles) and Yanic Konan Niederhäuser (foot) have progressed to playing 5-on-5 but will not travel with the Clippers to Phoenix.
body: Ingram and Niederhäuser, who have not played this season, continue to make progress in their respective recoveries. While both have been cleared to play 5-on-5, they won’t travel with the team to Phoenix for Tuesday’s game against the Suns. The Clippers play two home games to end the week; leaving Ingram and Niederhäuser in Los Angeles gives them more time to rehab at the team facility.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nikola Jokić (elbow) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Rockets.
body: Jokić is dealing with a sprained right elbow, but he hasn’t missed a game this season. If he can’t play on Monday, the Nuggets will likely turn to Marvin Bagley III to fill the void.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cameron Johnson (lower body) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Rockets.
body: Johnson, who has missed time this season with an ankle injury, played 29 minutes in Saturday’s win over the Pacers. If he can’t play on Monday, the Nuggets may turn to Bryce Hopkins to fill the resulting void in the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Aaron Gordon (lower body) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Rockets.
body: Gordon most recently played 27 minutes in Saturday’s win over the Pacers. He hasn’t missed a game this season, and Trevon Brazile is the likely replacement in the starting lineup if Gordon doesn’t play on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: DeMar DeRozan (back) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Rockets.
body: After missing Wednesday’s win over the Raptors with lower back spasms, DeRozan played 22 minutes in Saturday’s win over the Pacers. If available, he’ll likely take on a similar workload off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Christian Braun (calf) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Rockets.
body: The Nuggets return from Mexico City with a crowded injury report, as all six of their top players are questionable for Monday. If Braun can’t play, Spencer Jones could start, though his playing time may not increase much since Saturday’s game was his first of the season.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Richie Saunders (knee) is not on the injury report for Monday’s game against the Raptors.
body: Saunders, whose final season at BYU ended in February after a torn ACL, could make his NBA debut on Monday. The versatile wing was one of the best perimeter shooters in this draft class, and that’s an area where he could potentially provide value in Memphis. For now, Saunders should only be rostered in dynasty leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Stewart (knee) is out for Monday’s game against the Raptors.
body: Stewart remains out with a bone bruise in his right knee. That leaves Quinten Post to take on the backup center role behind starter Zach Edey.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Moussa Diabaté (quad) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Diabaté missed Friday’s loss to the Celtics, with Ryan Kalkbrenner replacing him in the starting lineup. That will likely be the case on Monday if Diabaté remains out.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brandon Miller (groin) is out for Monday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Miller left Friday’s loss to the Celtics with a sore right groin and has since been diagnosed with a strained right hip. The good news is that he’s considered day-to-day, so this may not sideline Miller for long. Tidjane Salaün picked up additional minutes on Friday and should play more with Miller out.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kon Knueppel (hamstring) will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
body: Knueppel strained his left hamstring before training camp and did not make his season debut until Wednesday. Unfortunately, he left after six minutes and has been diagnosed with another strain of the same hamstring. Knueppel’s absence should push Sion James back into the starting lineup, but he offers limited fantasy value as a streamer.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Thunder waived Dalen Terry.
body: Signed to a two-year deal on Tuesday, Terry has been waived to free up a roster spot for the recently acquired Nique Clifford. Terry’s waiver will not affect fantasy basketball or the Thunder’s rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Keegan Murray (ankle) is available for Sunday’s game against the Heat.
body: Sunday’s game will be Murray’s first since October 23. It’s unclear whether his playing time will be limited, but fantasy managers shouldn’t expect to see Murray’s minutes go well into the thirties. Precious Achiuwa has been the starting power forward in Murray’s absence.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Joel Embiid (foot) is available for Sunday’s game against the Bulls.
body: Embiid is set to play after the 76ers listed him as probable on the initial injury report. He’ll take on his usual role as the team’s starting center.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jalen Smith (finger) is available for Sunday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Smith was initially probable, so the status upgrade was expected. He’ll remain in the starting lineup, with Nic Claxton (hamstring) limited to 16-20 minutes in his Bulls debut.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Norman Powell (shoulder) is out for Sunday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Powell, added to the Bulls’ injury report Sunday morning, will sit out the matchup against the 76ers. As a result, Okoro will replace him in the starting lineup. Okoro is more valuable as a defender than as a scorer, especially in this particular matchup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nic Claxton (hamstring) is available for Sunday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Claxton is available to make his season debut after a preseason hamstring strain. He’ll come off the bench on Sunday, and the Bulls will limit him to 16-20 minutes. Jalen Smith remains the starter for now, but his fantasy value will take a hit once that changes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Gary Trent Jr. (illness) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Celtics.
body: After signing a four-year, $64 million contract in the offseason, Trent has more DNP-CDs (seven) than appearances (two) this season. If he can’t play on Sunday, his absence would not affect fantasy basketball or the Bucks’ rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Thunder acquired Nique Clifford from the Kings for two second-round picks.
body: The Thunder need depth after being hit hard by injuries, while Clifford gets a fresh start after falling out of the Kings’ rotation. As a rookie, the 24th overall pick in the 2025 draft averaged 8.6 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.4 assists in 25.1 minutes per game last season. Clifford averaged just over six minutes per game in eight appearances this season. Clifford may have a few more opportunities in Oklahoma City, a franchise that has developed young talent well over the years.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Mitchell Robinson (illness) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Robinson’s late addition to the Celtics’ injury report isn’t a good sign. If he can’t play, Neemias Queta and Luka Garza should see more minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Luka Dončić (back) is out for Sunday’s game against the Pistons.
body: Dončić will miss his second game of the season, the first being an October 28 win over the Clippers. Austin Reaves took on primary playmaking in that game and struggled, shooting 6-of-16 from the field and committing eight turnovers. As for the starting lineup, Quentin Grimes could replace Dončić.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Scottie Barnes (adductor) and Immanuel Quickley (hamstring) were limited at Sunday’s practice and will be questionable for Monday’s game against the Grizzlies.
body: Barnes and Quickley sat out Friday’s win over the Bucks, which led to Jakob Poeltl returning to the starting lineup and Jamal Shead filling in for Quickley. That’s likely to remain the case on Monday if Barnes and Quickley can’t play. The absences would also raise the fantasy ceilings of RJ Barrett, Ja’Kobe Walter and Collin Murray-Boyles.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Joan Beringer (nose) is available for Sunday’s game against the Jazz.
body: Beringer, who fractured his nose during Friday’s win over the Pelicans, is good to go for Sunday night. His availability means Trey Lyles’ playing time will likely decrease after he logged 29 minutes on Friday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jalen Duren (hamstring) has been cleared to begin on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in two weeks.
body: Duren strained his hamstring during Detroit’s second game of the season and hasn’t played since. The Pistons announced Sunday that the All-Star center is progressing in his recovery and has been cleared to begin on-court activities. Duren will be re-evaluated in two weeks. Paul Reed will remain the starting center until Duren is cleared to play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Keyonte George (illness) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: George is now questionable after not appearing on Utah’s initial injury report. If he can’t play, Isaiah Collier and Darryn Peterson stand to gain the most in playmaking responsibilities.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Norman Powell (shoulder) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Absent from the Bulls’ initial injury report, Powell was added Sunday morning due to right shoulder inflammation. If he can’t play, Isaac Okoro and Tre Jones should see more minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Julian Champagnie tallied 14 points (4-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, and four three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
body: Champagnie made four of the Spurs’ 17 three-pointers on Saturday, the second time this season he’s made at least that many in a game. While the rebounds were solid, Champagnie is most valuable to managers needing points and three-pointers. Tobias Harris’ continued absence makes Champagnie a little more important for offensive spacing reasons, but he’s only worth a look in deep leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Stephon Castle amassed 14 points (5-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, one block and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
body: Castle has scored in double figures in nine of 10 games this season, except for his scoreless effort in an October 31 win over the Timberwolves. Like the other starters, Castle did not play in the fourth quarter of Saturday’s victory, which likely robbed him of chances to post better numbers. His current value hasn’t aligned with his top-60 ADP, but Castle is closing in on the top-100 in eight- and nine-cat formats.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Devin Vassell notched 15 points (4-of-8 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
body: One of three Spurs starters to make multiple three-pointers, Vassell is averaging 1.6 per game this season. Despite his low field-goal percentage, the Spurs wing provides solid middle-round value in 12-team formats. With the Spurs playing four games next week, Vassell may be worth a look for those needing three-pointers and steals, as he’s available in 48 percent of Yahoo leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Victor Wembanyama finished Saturday’s rout of the Trail Blazers with 29 points (9-of-13 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers.
body: While the final stat line wasn’t as robust as his showing in Wednesday’s win over the Mavericks, Wembanyama thoroughly outplayed Portland’s Donovan Clingan on Saturday. The Spurs center only played 24 minutes, as San Antonio outscored Portland 87-56 in the second and third quarters. Wemby and the other Spurs starters watched the entire fourth quarter from the bench, which may have annoyed some fantasy managers hoping for an elite stat line. The Spurs play four games next week, starting with the Suns on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Scoot Henderson produced 13 points (4-of-10 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs.
body: Unfortunately for fantasy managers who believed a move into the starting lineup would improve Henderson’s value, he hasn’t delivered. Since Ja Morant (hamstring) went down in an October 29 loss to the Grizzlies, Scoot’s category-league value has ranked outside the top-300 in nine-cat formats. Unsurprisingly, Jrue Holiday (11 points, one steal and one three-pointer) has been far more valuable, regardless of league format. Portland plays three games next week, starting with a home back-to-back against the Thunder on Tuesday and Wednesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Damian Lillard finished Saturday’s loss to the Spurs with 12 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), seven assists and two three-pointers.
body: Lillard’s streak of games with at least 20 points ended at four on Saturday, with the veteran point guard also attempting a season-low eight shots from the field. Lillard shot a solid percentage from the field, but many expected more, especially with Ja Morant (hamstring) sidelined. The good news is that Lillard played both games of Portland’s back-to-back. Saturday’s game was a blowout, so he played only 20 minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Deni Avdija tallied 15 points (5-of-13 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, one assist, one steal and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs.
body: Avdija led the Trail Blazers in points and field-goal attempts on Saturday, but the overall stat line was underwhelming. Deni didn’t shoot well from the field and recorded just one assist. Surprisingly, Avdija’s fantasy value has slipped after Ja Morant’s hamstring injury. Over the last five games, he sits just outside the top-200 in nine-cat formats. Avdija will look to contribute more when Portland hosts Oklahoma City on Tuesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Yang Hansen finished Saturday’s loss to the Spurs with 12 points (3-of-7 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 10 rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer.
body: There’s no such thing as “garbage time"; those minutes are vital for non-rotation players looking to give their coaches a reason to call their name when the stakes are higher. While Yang’s showing against the Spurs is unlikely to make him a fixture in the Trail Blazers’ rotation, it was a step forward. The former first-round pick recorded his first double-double, establishing new career highs in points and rebounds. As good as it was to see him perform well, Yang should still be rostered only in dynasty leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Anthony Black finished Saturday’s overtime loss to the Warriors with 18 points (7-of-19 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, six assists, four steals, three blocks and two three-pointers.
body: Black didn’t have a great night shooting the basketball, but his final stat line included seven defensive contributions and six assists. Unfortunately, the Magic guard was not on the floor for the second half of overtime, as cramping sidelined Black with 2:47 remaining in the period. Orlando doesn’t play again until Tuesday against the Kings; hopefully, that’s enough time for Black to rehydrate and play without any issues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Stephen Curry exploded for a game-high 41 points (13-of-19 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), six rebounds and six assists across 36 minutes to lead the Warriors to a 126-119 overtime win against the Magic on Saturday.
body: Curry’s sublime start to the year continued in this one as he topped the 40-point plateau for the second time in eight games. His signature sequence came in the final minute of regulation when he knocked down a three-pointer before sinking a pair of free throws and converting a go-ahead layup in the closing seconds. He added five points in overtime as Golden State was finally able to pull away for good. The 38-year-old legend has delivered first-round fantasy value so far, averaging 31.3 points through eight games. Are you not entertained? The Warriors are in line for a three-game week that features matchups against the Pelicans, Rockets and Spurs.
author: George Bissell

headline: Franz Wagner delivered a team-high 30 points (11-of-22 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, 11 assists and two steals over 30 minutes in an overtime loss to the Warriors on Saturday.
body: Wagner continues to serve as Orlando’s main option with Paolo Banchero (ankle) likely out until at least late November. He knocked down just 3-of-7 from three-point range, but dished out double-digit assists for the fourth time in his last five contests. He’s averaging 20.8 points, 6.3 rebounds, 8.8 assists and 1.3 steals through nine games. The Magic have a three-game week on tap that features matchups against the Kings, Jazz and Bucks.
author: George Bissell

headline: Yaxel Lendeborg amassed 23 points (9-of-15 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and three blocks across 37 minutes in an overtime victory over the Magic on Saturday.
body: Lendeborg continues to be a revelation for Golden State, surpassing the 20-point plateau for the fifth time in 10 games to open his rookie campaign. He and franchise icon Stephen Curry combined for 64 points in a thrilling overtime victory, accounting for more than half of the Warriors’ offensive output. He came through in the clutch, scoring seven of his 23 points in overtime. The 24-year-old rookie sensation should be rostered in all fantasy formats, as he’s quickly establishing himself as a high-volume scoring threat in Golden State’s offense. The Warriors are in line for a three-game week that features matchups against the Pelicans, Rockets and Spurs.
author: George Bissell

headline: Wendell Carter Jr. contributed 19 points (6-of-12 FGs, 4-of-9 FTs), 11 rebounds and two blocks over 40 minutes during an overtime loss to the Warriors on Saturday.
body: Carter had little trouble handling an undersized Golden State squad to notch his second straight double-double. He was a perfect 3-for-3 from three-point range, but missed five times from the free-throw line in this one, which wound up mattering in a close contest. The 27-year-old former first-round pick has delivered fifth-round fantasy value this season, averaging 14.8 points, 9.6 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.1 steals and 0.7 blocks through nine games. The Magic have a three-game week on tap that features matchups against the Kings, Jazz and Bucks.
author: George Bissell

headline: Amen Thompson tallied 17 points (7-of-14 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, one steal and four blocks in Saturday’s loss to the Suns.
body: Thompson didn’t record an assist on Saturday, the first time that’s happened this season. The good news for fantasy managers is that he blocked four shots, double his total entering Saturday. While Thompson is providing top-100 value, his averages have decreased across the board compared to 2025-26. The Rockets open a four-game Week 4 on Monday against the Nuggets.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jabari Smith Jr. notched 15 points (7-of-12 FGs), nine rebounds, two assists, three steals, one block and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Suns.
body: Smith finished one rebound shy of a double-double and recorded a complete stat line in Saturday’s defeat. Over three weeks, the Rockets forward has provided top-25 value in 12-team formats. Given Smith’s fantasy production for most of his career, fantasy managers should look into what they can get for him. For the right return, selling high on Smith wouldn’t be a bad idea.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Fred VanVleet amassed 16 points (6-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, four assists, one block and four three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Suns.
body: VanVleet’s four three-pointers matched his season high, a number he’s hit on three occasions in eight games. The overall field-goal percentage pushed the Rockets’ point guard over 40 percent for the season, and that’s around where VanVleet has hovered for most of his career. Even with the low field-goal percentage, VanVleet does enough in other categories to provide reliable middle-round value when healthy.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kevin Durant finished Saturday’s loss to the Suns with 21 points (5-of-14 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), 10 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one three-pointer.
body: Durant had only one official field-goal attempt in the first half, scoring six points thanks to his going 4-of-5 from the foul line. He took 13 shots in the second half and made four, which hurt KD’s shooting efficiency. He did grab 10 rebounds, finishing with his first double-double of the season. The Rockets play four games next week, starting with the Nuggets on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander accumulated a game-high 30 points (11-of-20 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, nine assists and one block over 29 minutes to propel the Thunder to a 114-75 blowout win over the Wizards.
body: Gilgeous-Alexander scored 30 points in just three quarters to help Oklahoma City cruise to a relatively easy 39-point victory on the second night of a back-to-back. The 28-year-old scoring machine is averaging a sublime 29.9 points through 10 games, topping 30 points in exactly half of those contests. The Thunder are back in action with a busy four-game week that includes back-to-back showdowns against the Trail Blazers in addition to road tilts against the Clippers and Kings.
author: George Bissell

headline: Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori said on Saturday that Ja Morant (hamstring) “may not be out for as long as we thought.”
body: Morant, who suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain during an October 29 loss to the Grizzlies, was to be re-evaluated towards the end of November. However, according to Nori, a doctor in Los Angeles evaluated Morant and gave him a positive outlook on the injury. That’s good news for those rostering the athletic point guard, who was fitting in well with his new teammates at the time of the injury. Scoot Henderson will start until Morant is healthy enough to play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Andre Hunter (illness) is not on the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Heat.
body: Hunter did not play in Friday’s loss to the Spurs, with Leaky Black replacing him in the starting lineup. Black has played significant minutes recently due to his defensive ability, and that should remain the case on Sunday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Keegan Murray (ankle) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Heat.
body: Murray has not played since October 23 and has missed the Kings’ last seven games with a left ankle injury. Precious Achiuwa has replaced him in the starting lineup, and that should remain the case if Murray can’t play on Sunday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Jackson (groin) is out for Sunday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: A sore groin will keep Jackson out of Sunday’s game. His absence likely means the Clippers will turn to rookie Baba Miller as Brook Lopez’s backup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Yaxel Lendeborg, Gui Santos and Draymond Green will start Saturday’s game against the Magic.
body: Santos is back after missing the last two games with left knee tendinitis. His return means Will Richard will come off the bench after starting Thursday’s win over the Heat.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jordan Goodwin (calf) is out for Saturday’s game against the Rockets.
body: Goodwin will miss a third straight game while recovering from a right calf injury. Ryan Dunn has played more minutes in Goodwin’s absence but has not done enough to impact fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Rasheer Fleming (ankle) is available for Saturday’s game against the Rockets.
body: Fleming is available for Saturday’s game but has not been a regular in the Suns’ rotation. He should only be rostered in dynasty leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Onyeka Okongwu (throat) is available to return to Saturday’s game against the Nets.
body: Okongwu suffered a throat contusion early in the first quarter when he was inadvertently elbowed by Nets forward Julius Randle. The good news is that shortly after the Hawks listed Okongwu as questionable to return, he returned to the bench and got the all-clear. Zuby Ejiofor replaced Okongwu at the time of the injury.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Kenrich Williams, Aday Mara and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Saturday’s game against the Wizards.
body: The Thunder will start Saturday’s game with a bigger lineup, with Mara starting and Jared McCain coming off the bench. While the production hasn’t been consistent, Mara is worth the risk due to injuries to Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Larry Nance Jr. shot 5-of-7 from the field in Saturday’s loss to the Nuggets, scoring 15 points with two rebounds, one assist and five three-pointers.
body: Nance was in a groove on Saturday, matching his career high with five three-pointers. The veteran forward/center needed just seven attempts to reach that mark, a welcome development after Nance began the season shooting 5-for-17 from deep. He still can’t be relied on in most fantasy leagues, but Nance played 13 minutes while fellow reserve Jay Huff (zero points, three rebounds) played 10 minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: T.J. McConnell (hamstring) will not return to Saturday’s game against the Nuggets.
body: Making his first appearance of the season, McConnell played nine first-half minutes and finished with six points (3-of-5 FGs), two rebounds, one assist and one steal. He did not aggravate the hamstring injury; the plan is to bring the veteran point guard along slowly.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Anthony Davis (ankle) is out for Saturday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Davis will miss a second straight game due to his sprained right ankle. Deandre Ayton started Friday’s loss to the Hawks and played 23 minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nets head coach Jordi Fernandez said Saturday that Egor Dëmin (leg) is progressing in his recovery and will be re-evaluated next week.
body: Dëmin has missed the Nets’ last four games with a bruised right leg, and he’ll miss a few more before being re-evaluated. The second-year guard will miss games against the Hawks (Saturday) and the Mavericks (Sunday) before doctors re-evaluate his leg to assess his progress. Chaney Johnson has been the replacement in the starting lineup and should retain that role until Dëmin is allowed to return.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Noah Clowney (illness) is available for Saturday’s game against the Hawks.
body: Clowney is good to go after being listed as questionable on the Nets’ initial injury report. He’ll provide frontcourt depth off the bench but should not be rostered in most redraft leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cavaliers signed Riley Minix to a two-way contract.
body: Minix has appeared in 11 NBA games in three seasons, spending most of his time in the G League. The Cavaliers’ G League affiliate has retained his G League rights. To make room for Minix, the Cavaliers have waived Tristan Enaruna.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Lauri Markkanen (wrist) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Markkanen, who missed a game earlier this season with a sprained right wrist, is back on the injury report for the same reason. Josh Green replaced him in the starting lineup in an October 28 game against the Spurs and could do the same on Sunday if Markkanen can’t play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Joel Embiid (foot) is probable for Sunday’s game against the Bulls.
body: Embiid is on the 76ers’ injury report for plantar fascia injury management, but the probable tag suggests he’ll be available. If he can’t play, the 76ers may start without a center, with Dean Wade moving into the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Joan Beringer (nose) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Jazz.
body: Beringer exited Friday’s win over the Pelicans during the second quarter after suffering a fractured nose. Trey Lyles moved into the backup center role and may stay there if Beringer can’t play on Sunday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jalen Johnson (ankle) is available for Saturday’s game against the Nets.
body: Johnson is back after missing the Hawks’ last three games with a sprained ankle. His return likely means that Luguentz Dort will come off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Luka Dončić (back) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Pistons.
body: Dončić, who most recently scored 53 points in Friday’s win over the Trail Blazers, has been on an absolute tear over the last two weeks. If he can’t play on Sunday, Austin Reaves’ role would grow in importance, while Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton would likely see their minutes increase.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Joe (hip) is out for Sunday’s game against the Lakers.
body: Injured during an October 25 win over the 76ers, Joe has missed Detroit’s last five games. Sunday will push the unfortunate streak to six, with Kevin Huerter and Javonte Green among those who will continue to provide wing depth.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kyrie Irving (knee) is not on the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Nets.
body: Sunday’s game is the first of two in as many days for the Mavericks, who host the Pacers on Monday. With Irving available, fantasy managers should plan for the possibility that he doesn’t play against Indiana.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tarik Biberović (heel) is out for Sunday’s game against the Nets.
body: Biberović’s continued absence won’t affect fantasy basketball or the Mavericks’ rotation, especially with Santi Aldama making his season debut on Friday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Sergio de Larrea (knee) is out for Sunday’s game against the Nets.
body: De Larrea, expected to be re-evaluated on Saturday or Sunday, will miss another game. His continued absence won’t affect fantasy leagues, but de Larrea should still be rostered in dynasty formats.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tobe Awaka (knee) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Awaka did not play in Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks, and his availability won’t affect fantasy basketball on Sunday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jalen Smith (finger) is probable for Sunday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Smith is probable with a finger injury while Nic Claxton (hamstring) is questionable. If Claxton is out, Smith could return as the starting center once again.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Dailyn Swain (back) is out for Sunday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Swain will miss a second straight game with a back injury. His continued absence won’t affect redraft leagues, as the rookie hasn’t played consistent rotation minutes when healthy.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Zach Collins (illness) is out for Sunday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Collins will miss Sunday’s game with a respiratory illness. His absence won’t affect fantasy basketball, as the veteran center has played limited rotation minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: T.J. McConnell (hamstring) is available for Saturday’s game against the Nuggets.
body: McConnell is set to make his season debut Saturday against the Nuggets after missing the beginning of the season with a right hamstring strain. The Pacers are likely to ease him into his first game action of the year, but with Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) out he’s going to have fantasy value when he can play more minutes.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Desmond Bane (illness) is out for Saturday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Bane wasn’t on the initial injury report, but has been ruled out Saturday with an illness. With Jalen Suggs and Paolo Banchero also out, Franz Wagner should have all the usage he can handle against the Warriors Saturday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jaylin Williams (back) is out for Saturday’s game against the Wizards.
body: Williams is set to miss his third consecutive game with a back injury. Kenrich Williams moved into the starting lineup Friday against the Grizzlies, but he isn’t worth rostering in most fantasy leagues.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Anthony Davis (ankle) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Davis missed Friday’s game against the Hawks with a sprained right ankle. He’s questionable Saturday, so a return against the Thunder remains up in the air. Deandre Ayton started Friday and would likely start again if Davis remains sidelined.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jock Landale (hip) is out for Saturday’s game against the Nets.
body: Landale has missed the last three games with a hip injury. Zuby Ejiofor continues to soak up the vacated bench minutes in Landale’s absence. Ejiofor had 10 points, five rebounds and five assists in Friday’s win over the Wizards, but still isn’t playing enough to be relevant in redraft leagues.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jaylon Tyson (ankle) is out for Saturday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Tyson is set to miss his fifth consecutive game with a sprained right ankle. With Sam Merrill (elbow) also out, Tyrese Proctor and Meleek Thomas should see more minutes against the Knicks Saturday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Sam Merrill (elbow) is out for Saturday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Merrill left Friday’s game against the 76ers with an elbow injury in the first half and didn’t return. He’s listed as out for Saturday’s game against the Knicks with what the Cavaliers are calling right elbow injury management. Meleek Thomas could get the start in Merrill’s absence.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jarrett Allen (knee) is out for Saturday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Allen suffered a knee injury against the Thunder on Wednesday, didn’t return and hasn’t played since. He’ll miss his second consecutive game Saturday against the Knicks. Thomas Bryant will see more minutes off the bench while Evan Mobley slides over to center in the starting lineup.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jalen Johnson (ankle) is probable for Saturday’s game against the Nets.
body: Johnson has missed the last three games with a sprained left ankle. Listed as probable Saturday, the 24-year-old forward seems poised to return against the Nets. Luguentz Dort will likely head back to the bench with Johnson back in the lineup.
author: Nick Shlain
